It was observed by Truss and Miller that the cardinal characteristics add(M) and cof(M) can
be expressed in terms of the other cardinals of the Cicho´n diagram.
Theorem 2.6 ([Tru77], [Mil81]). add(M) = min {b, cov(M)} and cof(M) = max {d, non(M)}.
The same characterisation generalises to the higher Cicho´n diagram if we make strong enough
assumptions on κ. We note that this is not provable for all uncountable κ. For example, Brendle
[Bre22] showed that κ<κ < cof(Mκ), and thus max {dκ, non(Mκ)} < cof(Mκ) is consistent, and
holds whenever max {dκ, non(Mκ)} ≤κ<κ.
Theorem 2.7 ([Bre22]). add(Mκ) = min {bκ, cov(Mκ)} and cof(Mκ) ≥max {dκ, non(Mκ)}.
Under assumption of κ<κ = κ the inequality becomes an equality.
As for the other eight cardinal characteristics of the classical Cicho´n diagram, they appear to
be as independent as is possible in the following sense: any assignment of the cardinalities ℵ1 and
ℵ2 to the cardinals of the classical Cicho´n diagram compatible with both Theorem 2.6 and the
arrows in the diagram, is consistent (see [BJ95, Sections 7.5 and 7.6] for each of these cases). This
implies that the classical Cicho´n diagram is complete, as no arrows are missing from the diagram.
In fact, Goldstern, Kellner, Mej´ıa, and Shelah [GKMS21; GKS19] showed that all eight cardinal
characteristics can have mutually diﬀerent cardinalities within the same model.
